o1.biggest_strength: Branches the whole series on the quiz answer and leads with the 8.0% niacinamide path, keeps every email to one job, and pays off the sunscreen doubts with the real review line without inventing formula claims.
o1.biggest_mistake: Treats 'dullness' as part of the dark-spot block while the data shows dullness at 11%; fine, but it silently drops the 33% who bought sunscreen into a routine email that includes the acid wash even for sensitive users; and the WhatsApp gating on email clicks is optimistic where the pop-up opt-in is unproven.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: A stated end date or stated no-end-date logic laid out once so Email 5 and the WhatsApp timing line up cleanly, plus a short 'why this product' line per block so a beginner reading version B or C feels seen the way version A does.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharp data section up top and a strong email 1 that explains the naming philosophy honestly; the 14-day code expiry gives a real, non-fake reason to send the WhatsApp reminder.
o2.biggest_mistake: Email 5's routine puts the Salicylic Acid 2% face wash in everyone's morning and night, contradicting its own advice to sensitive skin, and it invents a 14-day code expiry the brief never stated; also mislabels the quiz shares (19% dryness+sensitivity is fine, but 55% for A lumps dullness in again).
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the expiry assumption out or state it as an assumption in the email 5 copy only, fix the 3-step routine so sensitive and dry subscribers don't get the acid wash, and move the email 2 product pick earlier so the code lands with a recommendation.

reason: Both are usable and on-voice, but Output 1 keeps the slow-start promise consistent and the code honest, while Output 2 writes a routine for everyone that quietly contradicts its own sensitive-skin advice and assumes an expiry date the brief never gave.
